children: November 24 (Renewables Now) - Spain’s Grenergy Renovables SA
has secured an investment-grade utility as the offtaker of almost 900 GWh of power annually from its Macarena and Locumba solar projects in Peru.

The companies have signed a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) with a 15-year term, Grenergy said on Tuesday without disclosing the name of its partner. It expects supplies from the two photovoltaic (PV) farms to begin in 2029.

According to Grenergy, this is the largest renewable energy PPA signed to date in Peru. It covers around 80% of the expected annual output of the 209-MW Macarena and 241-MW Locumba solar parks. To be installed in the southern regions of Ica and Tacna, respectively, they will together generate more than 1.1 TWh of electricity per year.

“Signing Peru’s largest renewable PPA marks another milestone for Grenergy and reinforces our commitment to the Andean region [..],” said David Ruiz de Andres, CEO of Grenergy. He also pointed out that the market offers strong solar resources and significant opportunities for the development of new renewable projects and their hybridisation with storage.
Grenergy has been active in Peru since 2015.

title: Grenergy bags long-term PPA for 450 MW of solar in Peru
